denomProfiles/evangelical-lutheran-churc: America's largest Lutheran church: mainline, ecumenical and socially engaged.
Accepts the Lutheran Confessions as true witnesses to the gospel.
Justification by grace through faith; Christ truly present in Holy Communion.
Scripture as the inspired Word of God, read with historical-critical scholarship.
Full communion with the Episcopal Church, several Reformed churches, the Moravians and the United Methodist Church.
Ecumenism: signed the 1999 Joint Declaration with Catholics through the LWF.
Social ministry through Lutheran Services in America and Lutheran Disaster Response.
Inclusion: ordaining women (in predecessor bodies since 1970) and, since 2009, partnered gay and lesbian clergy.
Racial justice and outreach in a largely white, Midwestern church.
Liturgical worship from Evangelical Lutheran Worship (2006); weekly communion is widespread.
Infant baptism and open communion for all baptised.
Bishops in the historic episcopate since Called to Common Mission (2001).
Synods (65) under an elected presiding bishop and a Churchwide Assembly.
North American Lutheran Church
Formed in 2010 by congregations leaving after the 2009 sexuality decisions.
Lutheran Congregations in Mission for Christ
Another network of departing congregations (2001).
Episcopal Church
Partner in full communion through Called to Common Mission.
Herbert Chilstrom
First presiding bishop (1987–1995)
Mark Hanson
Presiding bishop 2001–2013 and LWF president
Elizabeth Eaton
Presiding bishop from 2013, the first woman in the office
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/tagline: Ethiopia's fast-growing evangelical Lutheran church, the world's largest LWF member.
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/coreDoctrines: Evangelical Lutheran teaching: the Augsburg Confession and Luther's Small Catechism.
Salvation by grace through faith; Scripture as the only rule of faith.
Holistic or 'integral' ministry: serving the whole person, body and soul.
Open to the charismatic gifts, which revival made central to its worship.
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/focuses/0: Evangelism and church planting, especially in southern and western Ethiopia.
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/focuses/1: Development work: schools, clinics and water projects through its Development and Social Services Commission.
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/focuses/2: Ministry among Oromo and other southern peoples in their own languages.
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/focuses/3: Upholding conservative sexual ethics; it ended ties with the ELCA and Church of Sweden in 2013.
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/practices/0: Lively worship with Amharic, Oromo and local-language songs, prayer for healing and deliverance.
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/practices/1: Infant baptism alongside an expectation of personal faith.
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/practices/2: Strong lay evangelists and youth choirs.
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/practices/3: Synods led by presidents under a national church president; women ordained since 2000.
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/influenced/0/: Its growth helped make evangelicals a large minority in Ethiopia.
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/influenced/1/: Gudina Tumsa's 1972 letter on evangelism and development influenced LWF thinking.
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/keyFigures/1/: General secretary martyred under the Derg
denomProfiles/mekane-yesus/members/note: Lutheran World Federation statistics: over 10 million members, the largest LWF member church.
denomProfiles/hkbp/tagline: The great Batak church of North Sumatra, born of the Rhenish Mission.
denomProfiles/hkbp/coreDoctrines/0: Lutheran-based teaching; its 1951 Confession was the first confession written by an Asian church.
denomProfiles/hkbp/coreDoctrines/1: Salvation by grace through faith in Christ; Scripture as the Word of God.
denomProfiles/hkbp/coreDoctrines/2: The church's relationship to Batak custom (adat) is defined in its confession and church order.
denomProfiles/hkbp/coreDoctrines/3: Infant baptism and the real presence of Christ in Holy Communion.
denomProfiles/hkbp/focuses/0: Ministry among the Toba Batak in North Sumatra and in Indonesian cities.
denomProfiles/hkbp/focuses/1: Education, health care and the Nommensen University (founded 1954).
denomProfiles/hkbp/focuses/3: Engaging Indonesian national life as a large Christian minority.
denomProfiles/hkbp/practices/0: Worship according to the HKBP Agenda in Batak and Indonesian.
denomProfiles/hkbp/practices/1: Strong choirs and brass bands in congregational life.
denomProfiles/hkbp/practices/2: Hierarchical order: an ephorus with district praeses and pastors.
denomProfiles/hkbp/practices/3: Women ordained as pastors since the 1980s.
denomProfiles/hkbp/influenced/0/text: Daughter churches such as GKPI, HKI and the Simalungun church (GKPS).
denomProfiles/hkbp/influenced/1/text: One of the largest Protestant churches in South-East Asia.
denomProfiles/hkbp/keyFigures/1/role: American missionaries killed in Batak lands in 1834
denomProfiles/hkbp/keyFigures/2/role: Long-serving Batak ephorus after the church became independent
denomProfiles/laestadian/tagline: Northern revival stressing repentance, absolution and the fellowship of believers.
denomProfiles/laestadian/coreDoctrines/0: Living faith comes through the preached word and absolution spoken by a believer 'in Jesus' name and blood'.
denomProfiles/laestadian/coreDoctrines/1: Strong call to repentance, sparked by Laestadius's preaching against drunkenness.
denomProfiles/laestadian/coreDoctrines/2: Lutheran teaching on justification, with emphasis on the church as the communion of believers.
denomProfiles/laestadian/coreDoctrines/3: Conservative branches teach that true faith is found within their own fellowship.
denomProfiles/laestadian/coreDoctrines/4: Many conservative Laestadians reject contraception, seeing children as God's gift.
denomProfiles/laestadian/focuses/0: Personal repentance and the assurance of forgiveness.
denomProfiles/laestadian/focuses/2: Separation from worldly practices; some branches avoid television and alcohol.
denomProfiles/laestadian/focuses/3: Preaching by lay men, especially at large summer meetings.
denomProfiles/laestadian/practices/0: Mutual confession and absolution among believers.
denomProfiles/laestadian/practices/1: Services in prayer houses with lay sermons, alongside the Lutheran parish sacraments.
denomProfiles/laestadian/practices/2: Large annual summer services (e.g. Suviseurat in Finland) drawing tens of thousands.
denomProfiles/laestadian/practices/3: In early revival, ecstatic 'movements' (liikutukset) of joy during preaching.
denomProfiles/laestadian/influenced/1/te: Several North American denominations stem from the revival.
denomProfiles/laestadian/influenced/2/te: The revival profoundly shaped Sámi religious life.
denomProfiles/laestadian/keyFigures/2/ro: Sámi witness at the revival's origin
denomProfiles/reformed/tagline: Churches of Zwingli and Calvin: God's sovereignty, covenant and Scripture-shaped worship.
denomProfiles/reformed/coreDoctrines/0: The sovereignty and glory of God, including unconditional election (Canons of Dort, 1619).
denomProfiles/reformed/coreDoctrines/1: Scripture alone as the supreme authority, summarised in confessions such as the Heidelberg Catechism (1563).
denomProfiles/reformed/coreDoctrines/2: Covenant theology linking the Old and New Testaments and infant baptism.
denomProfiles/reformed/coreDoctrines/3: Christ spiritually present to believers in the Lord's Supper by the Holy Spirit.
denomProfiles/reformed/coreDoctrines/4: Church governed by elders and ministers in councils (consistories, presbyteries, synods).
denomProfiles/reformed/focuses/0: Preaching and the reform of worship by the 'regulative principle'.
denomProfiles/reformed/focuses/2: Transforming society and culture under God's law.
denomProfiles/reformed/focuses/3: Church discipline and the life of the congregation.
denomProfiles/reformed/practices/0: Simple worship focused on the sermon, with metrical psalms (e.g. the Genevan Psalter).
denomProfiles/reformed/practices/1: Infant baptism and the Lord's Supper celebrated with preparation and fencing of the table.
denomProfiles/reformed/practices/2: Elders and deacons ordained alongside ministers.
denomProfiles/reformed/practices/3: Removal of images, altars and many feast days.
denomProfiles/reformed/influenced/0/text: The British and American form of Reformed church.
denomProfiles/reformed/influenced/1/text: Puritan Reformed churches with congregational polity.
denomProfiles/reformed/influenced/2/text: Adopted Reformed theology while practising believer's baptism.
denomProfiles/reformed/influenced/3/text: Reformed theology shaped the Great Awakening.
denomProfiles/reformed/influenced/4/text: Reformed bodies joined unions such as the Church of South India.
denomProfiles/reformed/keyFigures/2/role: Author of the Second Helvetic Confession
denomProfiles/reformed/members/note: World Communion of Reformed Churches: about 100 million Christians in its member churches (which include Congregational, United and Waldensian bodies).
denomProfiles/reformed/inIndia: Reformed missions include the American Arcot Mission (Scudder family, Vellore) and the Welsh Calvinistic Methodists in the north-east (from 1841); much of this heritage is now in the Church of South India, the Church of North India and the Presbyterian Church of India.
denomProfiles/presbyterian/tagline: Reformed churches ruled by elders, shaped by Scotland and the Westminster Standards.
denomProfiles/presbyterian/coreDoctrines: The Westminster Confession of Faith (1646) and Larger and Shorter Catechisms as subordinate standards.
God's sovereign grace in election and salvation.
Scripture as the only infallible rule of faith and practice.
Christ the only head of the Church, ruling through elders in graded courts.
Infant baptism as a sign of the covenant; spiritual presence in the Lord's Supper.
denomProfiles/presbyterian/focuses/2: Overseas missions, especially in Korea, Ghana, Brazil and north-east India.
denomProfiles/presbyterian/practices/0: Sermon-centred worship, historically with psalm singing.
denomProfiles/presbyterian/practices/1: Kirk session, presbytery, synod and general assembly.
denomProfiles/presbyterian/practices/2: Communion seasons, historically with tokens and preparatory services.
denomProfiles/presbyterian/practices/3: Ordination of ruling elders as well as teaching elders (ministers).
denomProfiles/presbyterian/influenced/3/: Korea has some of the world's largest Presbyterian churches.
denomProfiles/presbyterian/influenced/4/: Grew out of Presbyterian frontier revivals.
denomProfiles/presbyterian/keyFigures/2/: Westminster commissioner and author of Lex, Rex
denomProfiles/presbyterian/inIndia: The Presbyterian Church of India, rooted in the Welsh mission begun at Sohra (Cherrapunji) in 1841, is a major church in Meghalaya and Mizoram; Scottish Presbyterian missions also shaped Indian education.
denomProfiles/congregationalist/tagline: Reformed churches in which each covenanted congregation governs itself under Christ.
denomProfiles/congregationalist/coreDoct: Each local church, gathered by covenant, is a complete church under Christ's headship.
Reformed theology, set out in the Savoy Declaration (1658) and Cambridge Platform (1648).
Scripture as the rule of faith and church order.
Infant baptism and the Lord's Supper as signs of the covenant.
Later liberal Congregationalism stressed freedom of conscience over confessions.
denomProfiles/congregationalist/focuses/: Liberty of the local church and the conscience.
Education: Harvard (1636) and Yale (1701) were Congregational foundations.
Overseas mission through the London Missionary Society (1795) and the American Board (1810).
denomProfiles/congregationalist/practice: Church meetings in which members choose ministers and decide church business.
Plain meeting houses and sermon-centred worship.
Voluntary associations or unions rather than binding courts.
Early ordination of women: Antoinette Brown (USA, 1853) and Constance Coltman (England, 1917).
denomProfiles/congregationalist/influenc: Early English Baptists emerged from Separatist congregations.
Many New England Congregational churches became Unitarian.
Congregational Christian Churches merged into it in 1957.
Jonathan Edwards led the Great Awakening from a Congregational pulpit.
denomProfiles/congregationalist/inIndia: The London Missionary Society, a Congregational body, built large churches in South Travancore (Kanyakumari) from Ringeltaube's arrival in 1806 and in Andhra; these joined the Church of South India in 1947.
